## Status markers

- ❌ **Not checked.** The entry has not been read, and its description here
  comes from memory or a search result.
- ⚠️ **Transcribed, unverified.** A checklist item or recommendation in a
  skill came from this source but has not been checked against it.
- ✅ **Checked.** Verified against the source.

On a reading-queue entry, ✅ means the question under the entry has been
answered, by reading the source or by deciding it is out of scope. Change a
marker when the check is done, not when the source is opened.

## Reading queue

The question under every entry is the same: which checks or recommendations
does this source give, and which topic in Section 3 of the specification do
they belong to?

### 1. Byon et al. 2013 — an internal population PK analysis guidance ❌

*CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology.* A company's account of writing
and using an internal guidance for population modeling. The closest published
precedent for this project; read first.

### 2. FDA 2022 — Population Pharmacokinetics, guidance for industry ❌

What the agency expects of a population PK analysis: data, model development,
evaluation and reporting.

### 3. EMA 2007 — Guideline on reporting the results of population pharmacokinetic analyses ❌

The European counterpart, on reporting.

### 4. ICH M15 — General principles for model-informed drug development ❌

Model risk, model credibility and the documentation a model analysis owes.
Check the status of the guideline before citing it.

### 5. Dykstra et al. 2015 — reporting guidelines for population PK analyses ❌

*Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics.* A reporting checklist
written by modelers.

### 6. Nguyen et al. 2017 — model evaluation of continuous data pharmacometric models ❌

*CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology.* The metrics and graphics for
evaluating a model, with what each one can and cannot show. The likely backbone
of a model evaluation skill.

### 7. Mould and Upton 2012 and 2013, Upton and Mould 2014 — population modeling tutorials ❌

*CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology*, three parts: basic concepts,
model building and evaluation, covariate modeling.

### 8. Bergstrand et al. 2011 — prediction-corrected visual predictive checks ❌

*The AAPS Journal.* The standard form of the visual predictive check where
dose or covariates differ across subjects.
